Mattel Launches Hot Wheels Racer Series Cars So Small and Cheap They'll Be Impossible to Ignore
8 photos
Photo: Mattel
Last year, toy maker Mattel decided to take the fight into LEGO's backyard by launching a new line of products called Brick Shop. The range of available products has constantly been growing ever since, and it presently counts tens of products. Until this week, though, there was no real entry-level line of toys available.
That changed after the company announced the release of the Hot Wheels Racer Series, a collection that blends together the Mattel way of doing things in plastic brick form with the glamour of Hot Wheels die-cast cars.
The collection that was launched this week counts no less than six vehicles, but the range is expected to grow to count as many as 20 models by the end of next year. They are all 1:64-scale, some of the smallest Brick Shop sets around, and so diverse they might very well make your head spin.
The collection includes, for instance, one of the most iconic models in Hot Wheels' history, the mighty Bone Shaker, which needs the correct assembly of 28 pieces of plastic to come together.
Then, from the 1990s, Mattel brings to life the 1991 Acura NSX (29 pieces) and the 1999 Honda S2000 (29 pieces). From closer to our time, the 2018 Audi TT RS enters the collection with 29 pieces, and so does the 29-piece 2024 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1. Finally, the Maserati MCPura wraps up the collection with 27 plastic pieces.
The above sets are entry-level not only on account of the number of pieces they require to come together, but also on account of their price. Every single one of them costs just $4.99, dirt cheap in the world of plastic brick toys.
Each of the six models will be offered complete with a metal base plate. Their wheels, fitted on metal axles, spin, and they are shod in rubber tires meant to bring them closer to their real-life siblings. Finally, each of the cars in this collection comes with its own distinct, custom pieces, that come together.
Mattel says the first examples in the Hot Wheels Racer Series will become available in January 2027, so a bit too late for parents and kids to enjoy them this Christmas. The launch dates for the remaining 14 models have not been announced yet, but we'll keep an eye on things and report back once we know more.
Those who wish to gift something from Mattel Brick Shop to their loved ones still have plenty of options available, including the recently introduced Mattel Brick Shop Original XBOX Console. The 1:1 replica of the original Microsoft XBOX from a quarter of a century ago is, obviously, a lot more expensive, selling for $329.99, and throws 3,509 plastic bricks onto the table to be properly assembled.
